key_insight: Rice husk ash yielded amorphous SiO₂ after chemical treatment and heating at 800 °C for 3 h, with subsequent annealing at 1200 °C producing quartz and cristobalite phases.
engineering_relevance: The synthesized silica offers a potential rice-husk-derived powder source for thermal spray coatings.
method: Chemically treat rice husk ash, then heat at 800 °C for 3 h.
Anneal the synthesized silica at 1200 °C to induce crystallization.
Characterize structure, bonding, and particle size using XRD, FTIR, and laser diffraction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports amorphous silica with D50 ≈ 88.9 μm, quartz and cristobalite formation after annealing, and Si–O–Si FTIR bands at 1000–1100 cm⁻¹.
watch_item: Thermal spray suitability remains unverified in the abstract, which reports no deposition trials or coating performance measurements.
paper_title: Synthesis of Amorphous and Crystalline Silicon Dioxide Powder Composites from Rice Husk Ash for Thermal Spray Deposit
